questions.question: At night, how far behind another vehicle should a motorcyclist stay?

options.text: Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.
Five seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds.
questions.explanation: It is harder to see and judge distance in the dark. Stay at least three seconds behind the vehicle in front of you at night. You need extra time to notice if the vehicle ahead stops and to slow down or stop.

questions.question: A helmet should NOT:

options.text: Meet U.S. DOT standards.
Fit snugly.
Have obvious defects.
Have been worn in a crash before.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have been worn in a crash before.
questions.explanation: A good helmet must meet U.S. DOT standards, fit snugly, and have no obvious damage. If a helmet was worn during a crash, replace it. A damaged helmet will not protect you.

questions.question: When it is raining, where is the safest place to ride?

options.text: In the center of the lane.
Off to the side of the road until it stops.
In the tire tracks left by cars.
At a higher speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: When it first rains, oil on the road makes it very slippery. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars because they are cleaner and have better grip. The left tire track is often the best choice.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Increase your speed.
Decrease your following distance.
Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther.
Wear tinted glasses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther.
questions.explanation: To stay safe at night, slow down and stay farther back from the vehicle in front of you. Use their headlights to see the road ahead. Change your lane position as needed, especially at night.

questions.question: Why should you practice using convex mirrors on your motorcycle?

options.text: Most people are not used to using mirrors.
They make objects look farther away than they really are.
They make objects look closer than they really are.
It is hard to remember to look at mirrors while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make objects look farther away than they really are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view than flat mirrors. However, they make objects appear farther away than they actually are. Get used to your mirrors before you ride.

questions.question: Where should a motorcycle rider position themselves in a lane?

options.text: Always in the same spot.
Change position based on road and traffic conditions.
Always in the center of the lane.
Always in the left part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Change where you ride in the lane based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: What does this signal mean?

options.text: Rest stop
High beams on
Turn right
Hazard

questions.correctAnswerText: Hazard
questions.explanation: When the lead rider extends their right leg, it signals there is a hazard on the right side of the road. This is an important group riding signal.

questions.question: How do you turn a motorcycle at higher speeds?

options.text: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
Press the grip opposite of the direction you want to turn.
Do not hold the grip because it is dangerous.
Do not lean the motorcycle because it is unsafe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the grip in the direction you want to turn.
questions.explanation: At speeds faster than walking, your motorcycle must lean to turn. Press the grip in the direction you want to go. This will make the motorcycle lean the right way.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: Applies some rear braking when you use the front brake.
Applies some front braking when you use the rear brake.
Applies equal braking to both wheels when either brake is used.
Remembers how hard you brake and learns your style.

questions.correctAnswerText: Applies some front braking when you use the rear brake.
questions.explanation: An integrated braking system automatically applies some front braking whenever you use the rear brake. Read your owner's manual to learn how your motorcycle's braking system works.

questions.question: How do you regain control if your rear tire locks up?

options.text: Release the rear brake.
Keep using the rear brake.
Swerve toward the side with fewer hazards.
Try to speed up while keeping the brake on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Let go of the rear brake to regain control of a locked rear wheel. However, if you lock the rear brake on a surface with good grip, you can keep it locked until you stop.

questions.question: Which vest or jacket color helps you be seen best?

options.text: Red
Black
Silver
Blue

questions.correctAnswerText: Red
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors when riding. Bright red, orange, yellow, and green are best. Dark colors are harder to see.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: At speeds greater than 55 mph.
After several hours of riding.
On short trips.
On long trips.

questions.correctAnswerText: On short trips.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles at speeds slower than 30 mph.

questions.question: How can you stop other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the left portion of a lane.
Ride in the center portion of a lane.
Give dirty looks if another driver moves into your lane.
Ride in a zigzag pattern to fill up a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of a lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane. This makes it harder for other drivers to squeeze in next to you.

questions.question: If your rear tire locks on a good road surface, what should you do?

options.text: Release and re-apply the rear brake.
Keep it locked until you completely stop.
Release the rear brake and only use the front brake.
Release the rear brake and use both brakes to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you completely stop.
questions.explanation: If your rear brake locks on a good road surface, keep it locked until you stop. You can still steer with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: How does a motorcycle's stopping distance compare to a car's?

options.text: Cars need much longer to stop.
Cars need a little longer to stop.
Motorcycles need longer to stop.
Both motorcycles and cars take about the same time to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both motorcycles and cars take about the same time to stop.
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, motorcycles and cars have nearly the same stopping distance. Wet or slippery roads make it harder for motorcycles to stop quickly.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When switching into neutral gear.
When you will slow down suddenly.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down suddenly.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before slowing suddenly. This warns a tailgater behind you that you are stopping to avoid a hazard.

questions.question: What headlight should you use in rain or fog?

options.text: Your high beam headlight.
Your low beam headlight.
Do not use your headlight.
Alternate between low and high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your low beam headlight.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in rain, snow, or fog. High beams reflect off these conditions and make it harder to see.

questions.question: How should you load cargo on a motorcycle?

options.text: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag.
Put lighter items near the front.
Try to not place items over the rear axle.
Place items behind the rear axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag.
questions.explanation: Load heavier items in front of the tank bag. Place cargo over or in front of the rear axle. Putting cargo behind the rear axle affects your control.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular in shape?

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black lettering. Follow the rules posted on these signs.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly while in a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Straighten up, square the handlebars, and stop.
Apply both brakes hard while leaning.
Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straighten up, square the handlebars, and stop.
questions.explanation: Straighten your motorcycle first, then stop. If you cannot straighten, apply brakes smoothly and gradually. Reduce your lean as you slow down, then increase brake pressure.

questions.question: A motorcycle passenger should:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before the engine starts.
Get on the motorcycle after the engine starts.
Sit as far back on the motorcycle as possible.
Hold onto the seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get on the motorcycle after the engine starts.
questions.explanation: A passenger should get on only after the engine has started and the transmission is in neutral. They should sit as far forward as possible without blocking the driver's control. They should hold onto the driver's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Which is NOT a benefit of riding in a tight group?

options.text: The group takes up less space on the road.
The group is easy to see.
The group is less likely to get separated.
Riders get to their destination faster in a tight group than in a spread-out group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders get to their destination faster in a tight group than in a spread-out group.
questions.explanation: A tight group is better because it takes up less road space, is easier to see, and riders stay together at traffic lights and during passes. Group speed is not affected by how close together riders are.

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Use only the rear brake.
Use only the front brake.
Use both brakes.
Use the rear brake hard while slowly increasing front brake pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, use both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
Body weight
How fast the alcohol was consumed
How often a person drinks alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often a person drinks alcohol
questions.explanation: Three main factors affect BAC: the amount of alcohol consumed, how quickly it was consumed, and body weight. Gender, physical condition, and food intake may also have some effect.

questions.question: As a driver, you should tell a passenger to do all of the following EXCEPT:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine has started.
Sit as far forward as possible.
Stay far away from you.
Keep their legs away from the muffler and chains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay far away from you.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to get on after the engine starts. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you and hold onto the passenger handholds or your waist, hips, or belt. They must keep their legs away from the muffler, chains, and other moving parts.
